title: Deploy with GitHub and Vercel
summary: First push, previews, variables, domains and production updates.

lessons.title: 1. Prepare a new project
lessons.concept: GitHub keeps your code. Vercel turns it into an accessible website.

explanation.text: Git records versions on your computer; GitHub hosts the repository; Vercel publishes a running version. L’ecomax is already connected: do not recreate its repository. For a new practice project, install Git and Node.js, create an empty private GitHub repository and open a terminal in the project folder.

Before staging, create .gitignore. Ignore .env and .env.*, node_modules, .next and .vercel; keep only an .env.example containing names and dummy values. Do not commit keys, customer exports or SQL backups containing personal data. .gitignore does not remove tracked files: if a key was published, revoke it and clean the history.

hints: GitHub keeps your code. Vercel turns it into an accessible website.
exercise.solution: With git status --ignored, .env.local should be ignored. No secret should be staged for commit.

summary: With git status --ignored, .env.local should be ignored. No secret should be staged for commit.

lessons.title: 2. Make your first push
lessons.concept: A commit is a local version. A push sends it to GitHub.

explanation.text: These commands are only for a new repository. Replace TON-COMPTE and TON-PROJET in the URL first. git add stages files; git diff --cached lets you review them; commit creates a local version; push uploads it to GitHub. Stop after diff to review the files and check for secrets.

Sign in with Git Credential Manager, GitHub CLI or SSH. Do not put a token in the URL. If origin already exists, inspect git remote -v instead of adding it again. If a push is rejected because the remote has advanced, fetch and integrate the changes; do not use force to bypass it.

codeExample.code:
git init
git branch -M main
git status
git add .
git diff --cached
git commit -m "Initial project"
git remote add origin https://github.com/TON-COMPTE/TON-PROJET.git
git push -u origin main

exercise.task: Run the commands one at a time in your new project. Pause at git diff --cached to review files.
hints: A commit is a local version. A push sends it to GitHub.
exercise.solution: After pushing, GitHub shows your commit and expected files. The site is not deployed to Vercel yet.

summary: After pushing, GitHub shows your commit and expected files. The site is not deployed to Vercel yet.

lessons.title: 3. Import into Vercel
lessons.concept: Vercel uses your repository and environment variables to build the site.

explanation.text: In Vercel: Add New → Project → connect GitHub → import the repository. Set Root Directory to the folder containing package.json and check Next.js detection. For L’ecomax, this is the website root, not mobile/. Check npm run build and keep the framework’s appropriate output settings.

Add variables in Project Settings → Environment Variables before deploying. Separate Development, Preview and Production; use a test database for previews. NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables become part of client code. Changing a variable requires a new deployment for that deployment to use it.

lessons.title: 4. Verify, connect the domain, publish
lessons.concept: A working URL must also show the correct data.

explanation.text: Wait for Ready, then open the deployment URL. Test mobile and desktop: pages, sign-in, products, images, APIs and admin access. If the build fails, read the first useful error in Build Logs. If pages work but data does not, inspect Runtime Logs and check variables, the Supabase project and permissions.

In Settings → Domains, add your domain and copy the exact DNS records requested by Vercel to your registrar. Preserve email records. Wait for verification and HTTPS. Add the domain to authentication and payment return URLs where required; check www and the primary domain.

lessons.title: 5. Update without losing your work
lessons.concept: A branch and preview let you check a change before publishing it.

explanation.text: For an existing project: inspect git status, create a branch, edit files, run tests and npm run build, then commit only intended files. Push the branch and open a GitHub pull request. Review the Vercel preview before merging into the configured production branch, usually main.

After merging, wait for Ready and verify that the domain serves the new deployment. If needed, restore a known deployment through Vercel, then fix the code in Git. Data and migrations do not automatically roll back. Success means one small visible change, an identifiable commit, a tested preview and that same change on the final domain.

codeExample.code:
git status
git switch -c learn/backend-guide
# Edit and test your files before continuing
npm run build
git add app/api/hello/route.ts
git diff --cached
git commit -m "Add learning API example"
git push -u origin learn/backend-guide

exercise.task: In your test project, change a heading on a branch, push it and compare the Vercel preview with the published site.
hints: A branch and preview let you check a change before publishing it.
exercise.solution: The new heading appears in the preview. Check it before merging into the production branch.
